bodyParts.name: Neck
bodyParts.description: Sides and back of the neck

bodyParts.name: Hips
bodyParts.description: Glutes, hip flexors and inner hips

stretches.name: Neck side bend
stretches.summary: Gently tilt your ear toward your shoulder.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder.
For a deeper stretch, rest your right hand lightly on the left side of your head.
Hold, breathing slowly, then return to centre and switch sides.
safety: Do not pull hard on your head – the weight of your hand is enough.
Keep the opposite shoulder down; don't shrug.
Stop if you feel tingling or numbness down your arm.

stretches.name: Look-down neck stretch
stretches.summary: Turn your nose toward your armpit to stretch the back of the neck.
steps: Sit tall and turn your head about 45° to the right.
Drop your chin, as if looking toward your right armpit.
Place your right hand on the back of your head and let its weight add a gentle stretch.
Hold, then slowly lift your head and repeat on the other side.
safety: Move slowly into and out of the stretch.
Keep the stretch mild – you should feel it along the back and side of the neck, not sharp pain.

stretches.name: Partner-assisted neck stretch
stretches.summary: Partner steadies your shoulder while you tilt your head away.
steps: Sit on a chair; your partner stands behind you.
Your partner rests one hand lightly on top of your left shoulder to keep it down.
Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder yourself – your partner does not push your head.
Hold, then come back to centre and switch sides.
safety: The partner only stabilises the shoulder – never press on the head or neck.
Agree on a clear 'stop' word before starting.
Not recommended if you have a recent neck injury.

stretches.name: Towel chin tuck
stretches.summary: Use a towel behind the neck to guide a gentle chin tuck.
steps: Sit tall and place a rolled towel behind your neck, holding one end in each hand.
Pull the towel ends gently forward to support your neck.
Glide your chin straight back, making a 'double chin', without tilting your head down.
Hold, then relax. You should feel a stretch at the base of the skull.
safety: Keep the movement small – this is a glide, not a nod.
The towel is for support, not for pulling your head.

stretches.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
stretches.summary: Draw one arm across your chest to stretch the back of the shoulder.
steps: Stand or sit tall.
Bring your right arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
Use your left forearm above (not on) the elbow to draw the arm closer to your body.
Hold, then switch arms.
safety: Keep your shoulder down, away from your ear.
Avoid pressing directly on the elbow joint.

stretches.name: Wall chest stretch
stretches.summary: Open the front of the shoulder and chest against a wall.
steps: Stand side-on to a wall and place your right palm on it at shoulder height, arm straight behind you.
Slowly turn your feet and body away from the wall until you feel a stretch across the chest and front of the shoulder.
Keep your chest lifted and breathe.
Hold, then turn back and switch sides.
safety: Rotate gently – don't force the shoulder backwards.
Lower your hand if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

stretches.name: Partner chest opener
stretches.summary: Partner gently draws your arms back to open the chest.
steps: Sit tall on the floor or a stool with your hands clasped behind your head.
Your partner stands behind you and holds your elbows.
Your partner slowly draws your elbows backward until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Hold, breathing slowly, then your partner releases gradually.
safety: Partner moves slowly and stops the moment you say so.
Don't let your head be pushed forward – keep your neck neutral.
Avoid if you have a history of shoulder dislocation.

stretches.name: Towel overhead stretch
stretches.summary: Hold a towel behind your back to stretch shoulders and triceps.
steps: Hold one end of a towel in your right hand and lift it overhead, letting the towel hang down your back.
Reach behind your lower back with your left hand and grab the other end.
Gently pull down with the left hand to stretch the right shoulder and triceps.
Then pull up with the right hand to stretch the left shoulder. Hold, then swap hands.
safety: Walk your hands closer together only as far as is comfortable.
Keep your back from arching – brace your stomach lightly.

stretches.name: Cat–cow
stretches.summary: Flow between rounding and arching your spine on hands and knees.
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Breathe in: let your belly lower and lift your chest and tailbone (cow).
Breathe out: round your back toward the ceiling and tuck your chin (cat).
Move slowly between the two positions for the full time.
safety: Move only within a pain-free range.
Place a folded towel under your knees if they're sensitive.

stretches.name: Child's pose
stretches.summary: Sit back onto your heels and reach forward to lengthen the back.
steps: Kneel on the floor with your big toes together and knees apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor.
Rest your forehead down and breathe into your back.
safety: Put a cushion between your heels and hips if your knees are tight.
Skip this if you have a knee injury.

stretches.name: Partner back pull
stretches.summary: Hold hands and lean back away from each other to stretch the upper back.
steps: Stand facing your partner, about an arm's length apart, feet hip-width.
Hold each other's wrists firmly.
Both bend your knees slightly and sit your hips back at the same time, rounding your upper backs.
Hold, then both stand up slowly together.
safety: Use a firm wrist grip so nobody slips.
Lean back at the same pace and come up together – never let go suddenly.
Choose a partner of a similar weight.

stretches.name: Foam roller upper-back extension
stretches.summary: Lean back over a foam roller to open the upper back.
steps: Sit on the floor with a foam roller behind you, across your upper back just below the shoulder blades.
Support your head with your hands, elbows pointing forward.
Keep your hips on the floor and gently lean back over the roller.
Hold, breathing out as you relax. Move the roller up a few centimetres and repeat if you like.
safety: Keep the roller on your upper and middle back – never under your lower back or neck.
Support your head the whole time.

stretches.name: Knee-to-chest
stretches.summary: Hug one knee in while lying on your back.
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Bring your right knee toward your chest, holding behind the thigh or on the shin.
Keep your lower back relaxed against the floor.
Hold, then lower and switch legs. You can also hug both knees together.
safety: Hold behind the thigh if you have knee problems.
Keep your head resting on the floor.

stretches.name: Lying spinal twist
stretches.summary: Let your knees drop to one side while your shoulders stay down.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms out wide in a T.
Keeping your knees together, slowly lower them to the right.
Turn your head to the left if it's comfortable.
Hold, then bring your knees back to centre and lower them to the other side.
safety: Keep both shoulders on the floor.
Place a pillow under your knees if they don't reach the floor.
Twist gently – avoid if twisting aggravates back pain.

stretches.name: Partner-assisted knee hug
stretches.summary: Partner gently supports both knees toward your chest.
steps: Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your chest.
Your partner kneels at your feet and places their hands on your shins.
Your partner leans in gently to bring your knees slightly closer, only as far as you guide them.
Hold, then your partner slowly releases.
safety: The partner applies very light pressure – this should never hurt.
Keep your tailbone on or near the floor.
Not suitable if you have a disc injury unless your physio approves it.

stretches.name: Exercise ball back drape
stretches.summary: Lie face-down over an exercise ball to round and relax the back.
steps: Kneel in front of an exercise ball.
Lie your stomach and chest over the ball, letting your back round.
Rest your hands or fingertips on the floor in front for balance.
Hold, breathing deeply into your lower back.
safety: Keep your knees or hands on the floor for stability at all times.
Use a ball that's the right size so you aren't overreaching.

stretches.name: Lying figure-four
stretches.summary: Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to stretch the glute.
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee, letting the right knee open out.
Lift your left foot off the floor and hold behind your left thigh.
Gently draw the left thigh toward you. Hold, then switch sides.
safety: Flex the top foot to protect the knee.
If you feel pain in the knee rather than the hip, ease off.

stretches.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
stretches.summary: A half-kneeling lunge to stretch the front of the hip.
steps: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front, both knees at about 90°.
Tuck your tailbone under slightly and squeeze your right glute.
Shift your hips forward a little until you feel a stretch at the front of the right hip.
Hold, keeping your chest tall, then switch sides.
safety: Put a cushion or folded towel under the back knee.
Don't let your lower back arch – the stretch comes from the tailbone tuck.

stretches.name: Partner butterfly stretch
stretches.summary: Partner gently presses your knees outward in a butterfly sit.
steps: Sit tall with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out to the sides.
Your partner kneels in front of you and places their hands on your inner knees.
Your partner presses gently and slowly toward the floor while you relax.
Hold, then your partner releases gradually.
safety: Pressure goes on the knees' inner side, never on the joint itself.
Use a 'stop' word and keep pressure light.
Avoid if you have groin or knee injuries.

stretches.name: Supported pigeon pose
stretches.summary: Pigeon pose with a block or cushion under the hip for support.
steps: From hands and knees, bring your right knee forward behind your right wrist, with the shin angled across your body.
Slide your left leg straight back.
Place a yoga block or cushion under your right hip so your hips stay level.
Stay upright or lower onto your forearms. Hold, then switch sides.
safety: Bring the front heel closer to your body if your knee complains.
Use more support under the hip rather than forcing it down.
Skip if you have a knee injury – use the lying figure-four instead.

stretches.name: Standing quad stretch
stretches.summary: Hold your foot behind you to stretch the front of the thigh.
steps: Stand tall next to a wall or chair for balance.
Bend your right knee and hold your right ankle behind you.
Keep your knees close together and tuck your tailbone slightly.
Hold, then switch legs.
safety: Hold the ankle, not the toes, to protect the knee.
Don't let your back arch or the knee drift out to the side.

stretches.name: Side-lying quad stretch
stretches.summary: Lying on your side makes this easier on balance.
steps: Lie on your left side with your head resting on your left arm.
Bend your right knee and hold your right ankle with your right hand.
Gently draw the heel toward your buttock, keeping your knees together.
Hold, then roll over and switch sides.
safety: If you can't reach your ankle, loop a towel around it.
Keep the stretch gentle – no pain in the knee.

stretches.name: Partner lying quad stretch
stretches.summary: Lie face-down while your partner slowly bends your knee.
steps: Lie face-down with your legs straight and forehead resting on your hands.
Your partner kneels beside you and holds your right ankle.
Your partner slowly bends your knee, bringing your heel toward your buttock until you say 'there'.
Hold, then your partner lowers the leg slowly. Switch sides.
safety: Partner moves slowly and stops as soon as you speak up.
Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
Avoid with a knee injury.

stretches.name: Strap quad stretch
stretches.summary: Use a strap to reach your foot while lying face-down.
steps: Lie face-down and loop a strap around your right ankle.
Hold the strap over your right shoulder with both hands.
Gently pull the strap to draw your heel toward your buttock.
Hold, then release and switch sides.
safety: Pull smoothly – no jerking.
Keep your hips on the floor and your lower back relaxed.

stretches.name: Seated hamstring stretch
stretches.summary: Reach toward one outstretched leg while seated.
steps: Sit on the floor with your right leg straight and the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh.
Sit tall, then hinge forward from your hips over the straight leg.
Reach toward your shin, ankle or foot – wherever you feel a stretch.
Hold, then switch legs.
safety: Lead with your chest, not your head, to avoid rounding your back.
A slight bend in the straight knee is fine.

stretches.name: Standing hamstring stretch
stretches.summary: Put one heel forward and hinge at the hips.
steps: Stand tall and step your right foot forward, heel on the floor and toes up.
Bend your left knee slightly and rest your hands on your left thigh.
Keeping your back straight, hinge forward from your hips until you feel the back of the right thigh.
Hold, then switch legs.
safety: Keep your back flat – don't round to reach further.
Hold on to a wall or chair if your balance is unsure.

stretches.name: Partner lying hamstring stretch
stretches.summary: Partner gently raises your straight leg while you lie on your back.
steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight.
Your partner kneels beside you, holding your right heel and resting a hand above your knee.
Your partner slowly raises your straight leg until you feel a stretch, and you say 'stop'.
Hold, then your partner lowers the leg slowly. Switch sides.
safety: Keep the other leg flat on the floor – your partner can steady it with their knee.
Partner never bounces or pushes past your 'stop'.
Stop immediately if you feel pain behind the knee or down the leg.

stretches.name: Strap lying hamstring stretch
stretches.summary: Loop a strap around your foot and raise your straight leg.
steps: Lie on your back with a strap looped around the ball of your right foot.
Hold the strap with both hands and straighten your right leg toward the ceiling.
Gently pull until you feel a stretch along the back of the thigh.
Hold, then lower and switch legs.
safety: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Bend the other knee with the foot flat if your lower back feels strained.

stretches.name: Wall calf stretch
stretches.summary: Lean into a wall with the back leg straight.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it at shoulder height.
Step your right foot back, keeping the leg straight and the heel down.
Bend your front knee and lean into the wall until you feel the upper calf.
Hold, then switch legs.
safety: Point your back toes straight forward.
Keep the back heel on the floor.

stretches.name: Bent-knee calf stretch
stretches.summary: Bend the back knee to target the lower calf.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it.
Step your right foot back a short distance.
Bend both knees, keeping the right heel on the floor.
Hold when you feel a stretch low in the calf, then switch legs.
safety: Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Ease off if you feel pain in the Achilles tendon.

stretches.name: Partner seated calf stretch
stretches.summary: Partner gently presses the ball of your foot toward your shin.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight.
Your partner kneels at your feet and cups your right heel with one hand.
With the other hand on the ball of your foot, your partner gently presses your toes toward you.
Hold, then release and switch legs.
safety: Partner presses on the ball of the foot, not the toes.
Use slow, steady pressure – never bounce.

stretches.name: Step heel drop
stretches.summary: Let your heels sink below a step to stretch the calves.
steps: Stand on the edge of a step with the balls of your feet on it and your heels hanging off.
Hold a railing or wall for balance.
Slowly lower your heels below the step until you feel the stretch.
Hold, then rise back up to level.
safety: Always hold on to something stable.
Lower slowly – don't drop or bounce.
Use the bottom step so a slip is harmless.
